1.q: מַדּ֤וּעַ אַתָּה֙ לְ⁠בַדֶּ֔⁠ךָ וְ⁠אִ֖ישׁ אֵ֥ין אִתָּֽ⁠ךְ
1.note: These two phrases mean basically the same thing. Ahimelech uses them together for emphasis. If it would be clearer in your language, you could combine them. Alternate translation: [Why have you come here all alone]

2.q: וַ⁠יֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗⁠י אִ֣ישׁ אַל־יֵ֧דַע מְא֛וּמָה אֶת־הַ⁠דָּבָ֛ר אֲשֶׁר־אָנֹכִ֥י שֹׁלֵֽחֲ⁠ךָ֖ וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִוִּיתִ֑⁠ךָ
2.note: If it would be clearer in your language, you could translate this so that there is not a quotation within a quotation. Alternate translation: [and has told me not to let anyone know anything about the matter for which he is sending me and about which he has commanded me]

3.note: The author is using a common expression of his culture. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [what do you have on hand] or [what do you have available]

David is using one part of himself, his **hand**, to mean all of him in the act of receiving. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [to me]

Ahimelech is leaving out some of the words that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You can supply these words from the context if that would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [The young men may have it if only they have kept themselves from women]

5.note: David is not referring to a specific **woman**. He means women in general. It may be more natural in your language to express this meaning by using a plural form. Alternate translation: [women have been kept from us]

If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [we have kept ourselves from women]
See how you translated this expression in 4:7. Alternate translation: [as in the past] or [as always]

David is using one part of the men’s bodies, their **vessels** (meaning their sexual organs), to mean all of them in the context of not having had sexual relations recently. If it would be helpful in your language, you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [the bodies of the men … with their bodies]

6.q: וַ⁠יִּתֶּן־ל֥⁠וֹ הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֖ן קֹ֑דֶשׁ כִּי֩ לֹא־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֜ם לֶ֗חֶם כִּֽי־אִם־לֶ֤חֶם הַ⁠פָּנִים֙ הַ⁠מּֽוּסָרִים֙ מִ⁠לִּ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה לָ⁠שׂוּם֙ לֶ֣חֶם חֹ֔ם בְּ⁠י֖וֹם הִלָּקְחֽ⁠וֹ
6.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [So since no bread was there if not the bread of the face having been removed from to the face of Yahweh to put hot bread on the day of its being taken away, the priest gave to him the holy]

The author is using the adjective **holy** as a noun to mean holy bread. Your language may use adjectives in the same way. If not, you can translate this with an equivalent phrase. Alternate translation: [holy bread]

6.q: כִּי֩ לֹא־הָ֨יָה שָׁ֜ם לֶ֗חֶם כִּֽי־אִם־לֶ֤חֶם הַ⁠פָּנִים֙
6.note: If it would appear in your language that the author was making a statement and then contradicting it, you could reword this as a positive statement. Alternate translation: [For the only bread that was there was the bread of the face]
See how you translated the term **face** in 1:12. Alternate translation: [the bread of the presence … from the presence of Yahweh]

7.q: וְ⁠שָׁ֡ם אִישׁ֩ מֵ⁠עַבְדֵ֨י שָׁא֜וּל בַּ⁠יּ֣וֹם הַ⁠ה֗וּא נֶעְצָר֙ לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֔ה וּ⁠שְׁמ֖⁠וֹ דֹּאֵ֣ג הָ⁠אֲדֹמִ֑י אַבִּ֥יר הָ⁠רֹעִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְ⁠שָׁאֽוּל
7.note: The author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

If your language does not use this passive form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. The context suggests that Doeg needed to stay at the sacred tent, which was in Nob at this time, in order to fulfill a vow or to wait out a period of ceremonial uncleanness. Alternate translation: [A religious obligation was detaining him]

7.q: וּ⁠שְׁמ֖⁠וֹ דֹּאֵ֣ג הָ⁠אֲדֹמִ֑י אַבִּ֥יר הָ⁠רֹעִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְ⁠שָׁאֽוּל
7.note: Here the author is introducing Doeg as a new participant in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation.

8.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 21:3. Alternate translation: [And would you have on hand a spear or a sword] or [And would you have a spear or sword available]

8.q: גַם־חַרְבִּ֤⁠י וְ⁠גַם־כֵּלַ⁠י֙ לֹֽא־לָקַ֣חְתִּי בְ⁠יָדִ֔⁠י כִּֽי־הָיָ֥ה דְבַר־הַ⁠מֶּ֖לֶךְ נָחֽוּץ
8.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. 9.q: אִם־אֹתָ֤⁠הּ תִּֽקַּח־לְ⁠ךָ֙ קָ֔ח כִּ֣י אֵ֥ין אַחֶ֛רֶת זוּלָתָ֖⁠הּ בָּ⁠זֶ֑ה
9.note: If it would be more natural in your language, you could reverse the order of these phrases, since the second phrase gives the reason for the result that the first phrase describes. Alternate translation: [since no other except it is in this place, if you would take it for yourself, take]

11.q: הֲ⁠לוֹא־זֶ֥ה דָוִ֖ד מֶ֣לֶךְ הָ⁠אָ֑רֶץ הֲ⁠ל֣וֹא לָ⁠זֶ֗ה יַעֲנ֤וּ בַ⁠מְּחֹלוֹת֙ לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ ב⁠אלפ⁠ו וְ⁠דָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו
11.note: The servants are using the question form for emphasis. If speakers of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [This David is the king of the land! Certainly they sing about him in the dances, saying, ‘Saul has struck his thousands, and David his myriads!’]
The servants mean **the land** of Israel. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the land of Israel]

11.q: לֵ⁠אמֹ֔ר הִכָּ֤ה שָׁאוּל֙ ב⁠אלפ⁠ו וְ⁠דָוִ֖ד בְּרִבְבֹתָֽיו
